title: IND-M - Flowserve Single Stage Mechanical Seal
description: In this course by CTE Skills you will become familiar with a Flowserve pump seal. The purpose of this video course is to provide you with a safe and correct way to disassemble, clean, inspect, and reassemble a Flowserve mechanical seal. A mechanical seal is a device that helps join systems or mechanisms together to prevent leaks, containing pressure, or excluding contamination. A typical seal rebuild can run up to $12,000, and the smallest mistake can cause a seal to fail, and turn into a costly project. Attention to detail is very important when working on a seal. This video course will teach you the steps to working with a Flowserve mechanical seal, including: *Determining what service the seal was removed from *Handling seal material safely, especially if it came from somewhere with hazardous chemicals *Removing the stationary face *Finding solutions while inspecting a seal *Looking for causes of failure This video tutorial brought to you by CTE Skills will go step-by-step into disassembling, cleaning, inspecting, and reassembling Flowserve mechanical seals. After you complete this 25 minute video tutorial, you will be able to correctly and safely deal with Flowserve mechanical seals in order to avoid costly mistakes.

The kinds of pumps described in this course are: -Piston pumps -Diaphragm pumps Using clear and descriptive graphics and diagrams this 4-minute course walks you through the parts and process of these different kinds of pumps. By labeling each individual part and showing you what it does step-by-step you get the opportunity to really examine how these pumps work. This video allows you to skip around, watch it multiple times, or watch it all the way through. Use this as a teaching skill or as a reference and come to understand these reciprocating pumps in only 4 short minutes!

title: IND-PTP - Jet Pumps
description: Jet pumps are used to lift liquids from wells. Specially designed jets are used to utilize the venturi effect, which is a drop in fluid pressure that results when an incompressible flows through a constricted section of pipe. In this short and simple course by CTE Skills Training, you will learn the basics in understanding jet pumps. In this course, you will learn: -The proper priming techniques of jet pumps needed in order for them to work correctly -The role a centrifugal pump has in the function of jet pumps -How to define venturi -The role of the foot valve In this three minute course, you will be subjected to knowledge with the help of animated simulations and audio narration. title: IND-PTP - Lobe Pumps
description: Lobe pumps, somewhat similar to external gear pumps, allow for fluid flow around the inside of their casing. The lobes in a lobe pump, however, do not make any contact. Lobe pumps have a variety of advantages, including high efficiency, reliability, and offer great sanitation. They are typically used in a variety of industries due to the fact that they can handle solids. In this simple course by CTE Skills, you will become familiar with the basics of lobe pumps and what they can and cannot do. In this course, you will learn: -The role of the gearbox and its external timing gears -The basic operations of a lobe pump -Lobe pump advantages and disadvantages In this three minute course, you will become familiar with lobe pumps in the most basic sense using animated simulations and audio narration. This course is simple and easy to follow. Once you finish this course you will have a much better grasp on learning about lobe pumps

title: IND-PTP - Vane Pumps
description: Vane pumps are positively-displaced pumps with two or more vanes attached to the rotor to move the liquid through the pump. Vanes are either sliding or flexible. In this simple course by CTE Skills Training, you will become familiar with the basics of vane pumps and what they can and cannot do. In this course, you will learn: -The components of a sliding vane pump -The components of a flexible vane pump In this two minute video course, you will learn through audio narration and animated simulations how to work with vane pumps. This course is simple and easy to follow in just a short amount of time! Get started today and become more knowledgeable on how to work with vane pumps.

title: IND-PTP - Gear Pumps
description: Gear pumps are positive displacement rotary pumps that transport high pressure, high volume flows. The two types of gear pumps include external and internal. In this course you will learn about the functions and purposes of gear pumps, as well as their overall advantages, uses, and limitations. In this course by CTE Skills, you will learn: -The purposes of an external pump, how it works, and its advantages and limits -The functions, body type, and advantages and disadvantages of an internal pump This 4 minute course uses audio narration and gear pump simulations to demonstrate both the external and internal types of gear pumps. Get started in enhancing your knowledge with this course from CTE Skills.

title: IND-PTP - Screw Pumps
description: Screw pumps are rotary, positive displacement pumps that can have one or more screws to transfer high or low viscosity fluids along an axis. A single screw rotary pump is also known as a progressive cavity (a PC pump). In this simple course by CTE Skills Training, you will become familiar with the basics of screw pumps and what they can and cannot do. In this course, you will learn about: -The role of the rotor -The advantages of progressive cavity pumps -The role of the motor and universal joint -How to describe what bearings do -About multi-screw pumps and if they have two or three rotors -Timing gears and bearings In this four minute course, you will learn about screw pumps in the most basic sense, using animated simulations and audio narrations to guide you along the way. This course is simple and easy to follow in just a short amount of time!

title: IND-PTP - Centrifugal Pumps
description: As the name might suggest, centrifugal pumps are a type of pump that operates on the principle of centrifugal force. This industrial training course on centrifugal pumps will provide you with a greater understanding of what centrifugal pumps are, how they operate, and why they’re used, along with describing the various parts of centrifugal pumps and the different forms and uses of such pumps. You will learn: -How to recognize common centrifugal parts and how they work -The roles of the volute, the impeller, and the suction eye -The workings of centrifugal pumps and the processes that enable them to work -Inlet priming The eight-minute learning experience is made engaging through this course’s use of animated simulations and audio narration. This course is conveniently available for your mobile phone or tablet/ After viewing this course, you will become much more familiar with centrifugal pumps and their applications.

title: IND-PTP - Axial Pumps
description: Axial Pumps move fluid in a straight line. Most axial pumps move in an elbow at the piping system. In this short course by CTE Skills Training, you will become familiar with working with axial pumps. In this course on axial pumps, you will learn the different purposes for the components of an axial pump, including drive shafts, propellers, mechanical seals, thrust bearings, radial bearings, and motors. The Working With Axial Pumps course uses animated simulations narrated with audio to enhance your knowledge on axial pumps. In a quick two minute tutorial, you will be able to grasp information on Axial Pumps in a fast and simple manner.

title: IND-PTP - An Introduction to Pumps
description: Pumps are devices used to move liquids or slurries. Liquids are moved from higher pressure to lower pressure, and overcome this pressure by adding energy to a system. Pumps can be classified as either being positive displacement, or dynamic. In this short course by CTE Skills Training, you will be given a basic introduction on pumps. In this course, you will learn: -The difference between a pump being classified as dynamic or positively displaced -The difference between axial forces and centrifugal forces for moving liquids -How to determine the difference between rotaries and reciprocating pumps -How to describe internal slip In this four minute course, you will get a great introduction to pumps using animated simulations as well as audio narration. When you finish this course, you will walk away feeling like you have a better grasp on the types of basic pumps.

title: IND-PTV - Diaphragm Valves
description: Diaphragm valves use an elastomeric diaphragm to separate the flow stream from the closure element. Diaphragm valves are a great choice for controlling the flow of fluids, containing suspended solids, and offer the flexibility of being installed in any position. The Weir type and the Straight Through types are covered in this course on understanding and working with diaphragm valves. In this course on the many uses and types of diaphragm valves, you will learn: -The body type and function of the Weir type valve -The body type and function of Non-Weir type valves -The advantages of a diaphragm valve -The limits of diaphragm valves This 2 minute video by CTE Skills uses audio narration and diaphragm valve simulations to show the advantages and disadvantages of diaphragm valves and their main functions.

title: IND-PTV - Plug Valves
description: Plug valves have a very simple design. Plug valves only consist of three components—the body, cover, and plug. In this simple and fast course by CTE Skills, you will begin to master and understand plug valves and their role. In this course, you will learn: -Plug operation and valve movement -The general uses of plug valves, including fuel gas systems, low pressure situations, slurry and lubrication, on/off applications, low temperature, and multiport operations -The purpose of the plug itself -About two-port and three-port plug valves In this three minute video, you will learn through animated simulations and audio narration how to work with plug valves. This course is simple and easy to follow in just a short amount of time. Get started today and learn how to work more closely with plug valves.

title: IND-PTV - Butterfly Valves
description: Butterfly valves are quick opening, quarter turn valves. Butterfly valves regulate or isolates flow in a manner very similar to that of a ball valve, but they are usually less expensive and lighter in weight, giving these valves an advantage and favorable preference in comparison to other valves. There are many different kinds of butterfly valves, and this course will help outline the different types and their functions. In this course you will learn about: *The different body types of butterfly valves, including wafer and lug *The disk of a butterfly valve *The different seats of a butterfly valve *The stem of a butterfly valve The Working With Butterfly Valves course uses graphical treatments and simulations narrated with audio to enhance your knowledge on butterfly valves. In a quick 4 minute tutorial, you will be able to grasp information on check valves in a fast and simple manner.

title: IND-PTV - Check Valves
description: A check valve is a valve that normally allows fluid to flow through it, and only in one direction. Check valves are two-port valves, meaning they have a port for inlet, and a port that acts as an outlet. Various types of check valves are used for different tasks, and most work automatically without any sort of external control. This course by CTE Skills will lead you through everything you need to know about the basics of using check valves. In this course you will learn about various types of valves, including: *Ball check valves *Swing check valves *Lift check valves *Stop check valves The Check Valves: The Basics course uses graphical treatments and simulations narrated with audio to enhance your knowledge on check valves. In a quick 4 minute tutorial, you will be able to grasp information on check valves in a fast and simple manner.

title: IND-PTV - Ball Valves
description: Pressure relief valves serve a key role in maintaining the safety and stability of oil & gas valve systems. Ball valves help control pressure in an oil & gas system which can pose harmful effects to equipment, potentially leading to equipment failure. Ball valves are particularly effective and desirable because of the fact that they are durable and last for years after the initial shutoff. Ball valves are quarter turn valves that have a round-closer element with matching rounded seats that create a tight seal. Ball valves are very versatile and are often used in shut-off applications. Ball valves are used to transfer gases, liquids, and “slurries”. In this course by CTE Skills, you will learn the different body styles of ball valves as well as their main purposes. In this course on understanding ball valves, you will learn: -The different body styles of ball valves, including single piece, two piece, and three piece -The various port styles of ball valves, including full port and standard/reduced port -How flow direction varies depending on port arrangement, including two-way direction and three-way direction In this 4 minute simulation video course, you will learn in a short amount of time the ins and outs of ball valves and their functions. Within this course, information on ball valves is presented in a clear and concise way. The information is easy to understand very accessible for any average person, not just industrial workers. Between the designs shown within the course and the audio narration, viewers come away with an enhanced understanding of ball valves.

title: IND-PTV - Globe Valves
description: Globe valves are an important fixture to understand because improper installation and operation can lead to leakage from piping, causing extensive damage and requiring maintenance. Globe valves are a highly common control valve. The simplicity of how globe valves are presented makes this course accessible and informative for industrial workers, new employees, safety and compliance officers, and anyone in general. In this course, you will learn: -The pressure drop that occurs during globe valves functions -The moving parts of a globe valve and how they work -The disc and seat types of globe valves In this three minute video, you will learn through animated simulations and audio narrations how to work with globe valves. This course is simple and easy to follow in just a short amount of time. Get started today and learn how to work more closely with globe valves.

title: IND-PTV - Gate Valves
description: To work in a construction-based, industrial workplace, it is integral to understand how various fixtures function and operate. Basic knowledge of such fixtures provides a means for employees to most effectively and safely complete their job and operate machinery. Gate valves are the most common type of valve and are therefore the most important valve for you to understand. This course will explain why gate valves are an important fixture to understand and how improper installation and operation can lead to pipe leakage that can cause damage and require maintenance to repair. This 3 minute long course uses video and audio narration to give you a thorough overview of gate valves in a time-effective and easy to understand manner. The simplicity of how gate valves are presented makes this course accessible and informative for industrial workers, new employees, safety and compliance officers, and anyone in general. This course describes the basic functions of a gate valve and the various components that comprise gate valves. Through a description of various ways to connect piping to the body of the valve to facilitate a flush seal, a demonstration of how the stem moves, and an explanation of the operation of the hand wheel itself, this course presents a wide range of important information on how gate valves function and are operated.

title: IND-PTV - Control Valves
description: Control valves regulate flow, pressure, temperature and liquid levels. These regulations are maintained through a process of partially or fully opening and closing valves. These control valves receive signals from controllers within the valves that monitor standard, normal conditions and compare those with the actual, fluctuating conditions. The opening and closing of the control valves is done through actuators. In this course, you will learn: -How pneumatic control valves, electrical control valves, and hydraulic control valves work -Demonstrations of control valve functions In this short video, you will learn through animated simulations and audio narrations how to work with control valves. This course is not just for industrial workers, in fact, it is simple enough for the common person to understand. Get started today and learn all about control valves.

title: IND-PTV - Pressure Relief Valves
description: Pressure relief valves serve a major role in maintaining the safety and stability of oil and gas valve systems. These relief valves help control the pressure in oil and gas systems which can pose harmful threats to equipment, that if not checked can potentially lead to equipment failure. This safety relief valve course takes about seven minutes of your time while teaching you through audio narration and videos. The course highlights main points by elaborating on certain aspects of relief valve systems, such as the comprehensive designs and important terminology. This pressure relief valve course provides oil and gas companies with a great, time-effective overview of safety valves that includes explaining the basic functions of relief valves and the main parts of relief valves. The course describes safety relief valves and outlines the functions of these different valves and provides you with a thorough understanding of all their basic functions.

title: HST-AP Introduction to the Muscular System
description: The muscular system is made up of over 600 muscles. While we won’t be covering all 600 individual muscles in this overview video, we will be discussing the … - Main functions of the muscular system - 5 major properties of the muscular system - 5 types of muscle movements withing the muscular system - 3 types of muscles within the muscular system - and how all of this works together to make up the muscular system. The primary purpose for the Muscular system is to provide movement for the body. The muscles receive their ability to move the body through the nervous system. Now there is much more to discuss about the muscular system but that’s as far as we will go in this introductory video. After watching this video you should at least have a basic understanding of what makes up the muscular system, its properties and functions. For a more in depth study of the muscular system, look for future CTE videos where we will cover topics such as the 14 major muscle groups, as well as topics such as common diseases and conditions specific to the muscular system.

title: HST-AP Introduction to the Cardiovascular System
description: The cardiovascular system, also known as the circulatory system, is the transportation system of the body. The major structures that make this possible are the heart, blood vessels and blood. Simply put, the heart pumps the blood in order to move nutrients through the blood vessels to nourish and to remove metabolic wastes from the body. The purpose of this video is to present a basic understanding of the Cardiovascular System. A more in depth study of the system will be presented in other CTE videos where we will look into each specific structure and function of the Cardiovascular system. After watching this video, you should have a basic understanding of what the Cardiovascular System is, the basic functions, and the basic structures that define the heart.

title: HST-AP Introduction to the Respiratory System
description: The Respiratory System plays a major part in our survival and works hand in hand with the Circulatory System. Respiration for the body can not happen without the circulation of the blood driven by the cardiovascular system. Simply said, it is through the respiratory structures that Oxygen (a gas) is directed to the lungs and passed into the blood transportation system which then delivers the Oxygen to the body. But this is just half the trip. In this short video about the Respiratory System, we will discuss how a breath of fresh air is taken in through the respiratory pathway by the following structures...t he nose, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi tubes, and the lungs including the alveoli. All of this will be explained in this easy to understand detailed animation of the Respiratory System.

title: HST-AP Introduction to the Digestive System
description: The Digestive System is also known as the “gastrointestinal system”. This system fulfills two of the basic and essential requirements for being alive… Food intake and Waste elimination. In this video we will be discussing the functions of the Digestive System, the connection with the immune system, the components and accessory organs that make it up, as well as the process of digestion. The components of the Digestive System are classified by two major functions. Absorption of Nutrients and Elimination of Waste.

title: HST-AP Introduction to the Urinary System
description: The Urinary, or Excretory System is another system by which the body rids itself of unwanted Toxins or (waste). Basically, the urinary system’s main purpose is to maintain the body’s “homeostasis”. In other words, the urinary system’s main function is to maintain the body’s acid-base balance. It is important to know, the human organism was meant to stay healthy and systems such as the urinary, digestive, skin, and other vital organ systems were created for that purpose. They are designed to keep the body healthy and able to withstand diseases. But if the load of Toxins and/or waste is greater than what these systems can handle, guess what happens. You can learn more about this, by watching CTE skills’ “Introduction to the Cell” and see how disease is created. In this introductory video on the urinary system however, we’ll just be taking a look at The purpose of the Urinary System The structures that make it up The functions of each And how they work together to maintain balance in the body

description: There are multiple ways to cut tubing but they won’t all work in every situation. There are pros and cons to consider for each. Some of the methods for cutting the tube include a hand tube cutter, a hacksaw, or a chop saw. Watch and found out which tools work best in each circumstance.

title: IND-I Tube Bending Preparation
description: Before we bend a tube there are certain steps we must take in preparation and it’s helpful to know what will happen to the tube itself during bending. You’ll also need to understand the proper operation of a Manual Hand Tube Bender as well as how to measure the tubing and how to plan out the tube line.

title: IND-I Making the Bend
description: You should now have a better understanding of the tubing itself and the basic operation of a tube bender. Now we can begin to measure and start the bending process of fabricating a tube line. This video will cover measuring and marking the tube, placing the tube in the bender, making the bend, checking for square, improper tube bending, proper tube bending, proper 90 degree bends, and measuring the tube centerline.

title: IND-I Bend Direction Mark
description: Most tube lines will not be limited to just one bend. There will be many items and obstacle you will have to work around. In this CTE video we will explore the many things you will need to consider in making multiple bends in your tubing line. Some of the topics discussed will be making the proper measurements, adding a bend direction mark, proper tube alignment, making the bend, and checking the angularity.

title: IND-I Tube Gain
description: Most tube lines will not be limited to just one bend. There will be many items and obstacles you will have to work around. In this CTE video we will show you a third bend in this tubing line and explore the many things you will need to consider in making multiple bends in your tubing line. Some of the topics discussed will be making the proper measurements, tube gain calculation, proper tube alignment and preparation, making the bend, and checking the angularity.

title: IND-I Changing Planes and Tube Orientation
description: Most tube lines will not be limited to just one bend. There will be many items and obstacles you will have to work around. To this point in the CTE Tube Bending series, we’ve been bending on only one plane. In this video we’ll do our final bend but this we’ll show you how to do it on a different plane. Some of the topics discussed will be making the proper measurements, tube orientation, changing planes, proper tube alignment and preparation, making the bend, and checking the angularity.

title: IND-I Tube Fitting Assembly
description: Tubing is just tubing if it isn’t working together with instrumentation and different systems. It would also be impossible to fabricate the tubing line with just one piece of tubing. Each piece of tubing will need to be connected to the next piece. In order to do that we need tube fittings. These fittings must be precisely used in order to function properly and to create a gas tight seal. In this video we will cover topics such as component orientation, tube insertion, makeup procedure, port connectors and plugs, remake procedures, and fitting performance and troubleshooting.

title: HST-AP Introduction to The Nervous System
description: The basic purpose of the Nervous System is to coordinate all of the activities of the body. It enables the Body to respond and adapt to changes that occur both inside and outside the body. The two major parts to the Nervous System are the Central Nervous System and the Peripheral Nervous System. The Central Nervous System is also divided into two major structures. The Brain and the Spinal Cord. The Brain is found within the skull, or cranium and it is made up of 6 main sections. These six are the Cerebrum, Cerebellum, Diencephalon, the Midbrain, Pons, and the Medulla Oblongata. The other half of the Central Nervous System is the Spinal Cord. The spinal cord is the link between the brain and the nerves in the rest of your body. The spinal cord is divided into four different regions: the cervical, thoracic, lumbar and, afferent and efferent spinal nerves, which merge to form peripheral nerves. Now that we know the Brain and Spinal Cord primarily make up the Central Nervous System, let’s look at the Peripheral Nervous System. The Peripheral Nervous System is essentially, the Nervous System outside of the brain and spinal cord. The Peripheral Nervous System is subdivided into two smaller systems called the Somatic Nervous System, and the Autonomic Nervous System. Watch this CTE video on the Nervous System to gain a more in depth and visual understanding.

title: HVAC-B Introduction to HVAC
description: The Heating Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) field is growing and we have a shortage of good technicians to handle this work. In this CTE video series on HVAC, we will begin by taking a look at Air Flow, Ducts and System design. This seems to be one of the most misunderstood areas in this industry. Whether you are working in commercial, industrial, or residential systems, air flow continues to be one of the biggest challenges in maintaining an efficient system.

title: HVAC-B Typical Problems
description: Working in the HVAC industry you will receive various types of complaints throughout the summer about a system not cooling well. One of the first things people do, but probably the last thing they should, is start adding freon. What you should typically be doing first is checking the duct system and looking for air leaks. Some of the problems you might see with this are...increased utility costs, houses with significant amount of dust, and allergy problems. Leaks in the return air can be just as bad. These leaks could be sucking in 150 degree air into the system. Noise complaints are another problem you might encounter from having a poorly designed system which could cause you to have too much air flow out of a duct. Other Duct and System Design problems include sweat or condensation on grills, hot or cold spots, or dust.

title: HVAC-B Return Air Grills
description: The Heating Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) field is growing and we have a shortage of good technicians to handle this work. In this CTE video beginner series on HVAC, we will begin by taking a look at Air Flow, Ducts and System design. This seems to be one of the most misunderstood areas in this industry. Whether you are working in commercial, industrial, or residential systems, air flow continues to be one of the biggest challenges in maintaining an efficient system.

title: HVAC-B Static Pressure & Noise
description: Noise in an AC system is usually due to excess air coming through the ducts. In a properly designed air system you will not be able to see, hear, or feel air blowing anywhere. It should just be a comfortable room. Static Pressure is a pressure in the duct system that is created by the systems fan. The higher the static pressure, the slower the velocity of air.

title: HVAC-B Supply Grills
description: Grills are the most familiar part of an HVAC system. It's something everyone can recognize. What you might not know is how important of a role they play in system design. Grills don't just direct the airflow but they are also a part of creating the overall static pressure. These grills are equipped with dampers in order to help control the airflow. Closing off these dampers however might not be the best thing for they room you are in.

title: HVAC-B AC Filters
description: Will you filter pass the salt Test? Many complaints from customers revolve around dust in the home. This usually is the result of a duct system leak. That's not always the case though. Poor air filters can also be at fault. A lot of times people will just buy the cheapest filter they can find not understanding the consequences.

title: HVAC-B Return Air
description: Having the return air sized properly is very important in getting the correct static pressure. A general rule of thumb is 12"x12" per ton of air conditioning. In other words, 1 square foot of return per ton of AC unit. In addition to the size of the return air, the filter plays a big role in static pressure and the velocity as well. Filters are given a MERS rating. Find out what that means and more in this CTE video.

title: HVAC-B Flex Duct
description: Flex duct in inherently, by its name, is flexible. It allows us to move and bend it in any direction. Flex duct is typically best for shorter runs. If flex duct is used for longer runs you can begin to lose air flow. Watch this CTE video to learn the proper uses and installation methods for flex duct.

title: HVAC-B Elements of a Duct System
description: A duct system is made up of many different components. In this video Robert will be covering some of the elements of a duct system in order to give you a better understanding and a visual of what actually happens inside a duct system with air flow.

title: HVAC-B Insulated Box
description: An insulated box is one of the many elements in a duct system. This is one of the last components the air will flow through before being dispersed into the home by a three way grill. The box is insulated on the inside to prevent condensation from forming. Learn more about the proper use and installation of the insulated box with this CTE video.

title: HVAC-B New Home Construction
description: Many times in new home construction the contractor will go with the lowest bid to install the Air System. Too many times they end up with bad results. Correct installation and a properly sized unit are key in installing a system that will run effectively and save money. In this CTE video, Robert Currie with Innovative Air Solutions explains some of the key factors in getting this right for the customer.

title: HVAC-B System Duct Leaks
description: Many HVAC technicians don't realize how catastrophic duct leaks can be to a home. There is more to it than just having cold air leak out into your attic. The loss of air has to be made up somewhere. That typically means your system will be taking in more outside air through cracks and doors of the home. This can begin to put a real strain on your system and make it difficult to properly cool or heat a home. Listen to Robert in this CTE video as he explains the real problem with duct leaks.

title: HVAC-B Heat Transfer
description: If you are a student taking an AC class or refrigeration class then heat transfer is something you will eventually come across. Simply put, heat transfer is taking heat from one space and moving it to another. In essence, an AC technician is responsible for transferring heat from inside of a home or a building to the outside. In this CTE video, Robert discusses different sources of heat and how to deal with them.

title: HVAC-B Heat Load Factors
description: As mentioned in an earlier CTE video about AC systems, any air leaked out of a system will naturally cause more air to pulled in. This will typically be warm outside air. This along with many other factors play into your heat load calculation. Things such as ceiling height or level of insulation are just a couple. Learn more about these and other heat load factors in the CTE video.

title: HVAC-B Heat Load Examples
description: Sometimes working as an HVAC Technician you need to understand several other trades as well. At times you may need to be part Building Contractor to understand some of the aspects of a home and how they affect heat transfer. Check out this HVAC video with Robert from Innovative Air Solutions to get a better understanding of these Heat Load examples.

title: HVAC-B Heat Load Designs
description: What do heat loads look like on paper? In this CTE video Robert will go over the specifics of a heat load report. For heat load purposes there are certain design criteria that must be taken into consideration. In this CTE video, Robert explains all that a heat load report entails and how it plays into design.

title: HVAC-B Heat Load Data & Causes
description: In the previous video we discussed the design conditions that apply to heat loads. In this video we will discuss the calculations involved in heat loads. One very important piece of data to keep in mind is accurate weather data. Different areas of the country will design according to different climates.

title: HVAC-B Duct Sizing Calculations
description: So far in this series on Duct and System Design we have discussed heat transfer, duct leaks, and heat load calculations. With an understanding of the system and the data collected we are able to properly design a system. Part of this design is calculating duct size. This is done using the metric of CFM. CFM is simply cubic feet per minute. So how does this all tie together? In this CTE video, Robert explains how to use a duct wheel to calculate the proper duct size for a given system.

title: HVAC-B Surge Protectors
description: In the past, most AC systems were truly mechanical with very few electrical components. Now days though, what protects your AC unit if a storm rolls through, you have power surges or spikes, or anything that disrupts our normal power to the unit. Surge protectors are a very important component in protecting your system and all of its electrical components. Watch as Robert explains the difference between standard surge protectors and the ones we need for our air systems.

title: HVAC-B Capacitors
description: Capacitors are a simple, yet fragile component in an AC system. A capacitor is an energy storing device. It is a medium by which energy is stored to either be released suddenly or over a period of time. The capacitor in your AC system consists of 3 terminals. These 3 terminals are common, hermetic, and fan. In this CTE video Robert explains why it is a good idea to have these checked periodically. He'll also cover the different ratings and how to understand them.

title: HVAC-B Contactors
description: A contactor is nothing more than an on and off switch for an outside unit. The power is connected and comes in, then various components such as compressors and fan motors are connected for power to come out. These contactors are rated by the voltage of the coils. When working with a contactor, it's not only important to have the correct voltage, but also that the wires are connected and disconnected at the correct terminals. In this CTE video Robert explains why and what the damaging results could be if not done properly.

title: HVAC-B Transformers
description: A transformer is a component that takes incoming power and transforms it into the appropriate voltage needed for a system. In a typical residential HVAC system, it will provide 24 volts. On a transformer you will see several wires all with different colors. It may look confusing at first, but in this CTE video Robert explains the difference and purpose of each. You'll also learn about the different voltages for each.

title: HVAC-B Blower Motors
description: In this CTE video, Robert will be talking about a quarter horse, 115 volt reversible blower motor. He'll be discussing the different wires and what there purpose is as well as the operational functions of the motor itself. You'll also learn the difference between a condenser motor and an evaporator motor. It is very important not to confuse the two.

title: HVAC-B Condenser Motors
description: In a previous CTE video Robert covered a blower motor which was classified as an evaporator motor. In this video we'll discuss the condenser motor. You'll learn to identify the difference between the two and also understand the purpose of each. This particular motor is a one third to one sixth horse power 1075 RPM motor. On a condenser motor it is important to notice the difference in RPM. Frame size is another important factor to understand. Find out why and more in this latest CTE HVAC video with Robert Currie from Innovative Air Solutions.

title: HVAC-B Run Capacitors
description: In a previous CTE video we discussed that a capacitor is an energy storing device. In this particular video, we will talk more specifically about a Run Capacitor. The Run Capacitor provides an extra leg of power to a motor. This could be a fan motor on an outside unit, a blower motor on an inside unit, or even for a compressor. Each capacitor has is own microfarad rating. These ratings are important in understanding the correct capacitor for any situation.

title: HVAC-B Relays
description: A relay is nothing more than a device to send power from one place to the next or to relay power. A relay is not limited to but typically used on fan motor operations. The relay consists of a coil, which is used to energize the relay and multiple leads. Learn the basic operation and uses of a relay in an AC or HVAC system in this latest CTE video on HVAC components.

title: HVAC-B Sequencers
description: An HVAC sequencer is a small circuit designed to help stabilize circuits and turn switches on and off quickly in an electrical setting. In this particular video we will be covering a heat sequencer. This device will typically run our fan or indoor blower motor on air handler applications. It can also turn on and off our electric heat strips. It is a very simple device but very powerful in what it does. Watch this CTE video on the Heat Sequencer and learn the structure of how it is made and it's basic operation. You'll also learn some of the typical failures you'll find with this device.

title: HVAC-B Slinky
description: In this CTE video Robert discusses a heating element known as a slinky. So what does a Slinky have to do with HVAC? Called this for its obvious resemblance to the famous toy, what it does is hold its shape when stretched. This device is what makes our electric heating systems work. The slinky acts as a giant resistor when power is applied. Watch this CTE video with Robert Currie from Innovative Air Solutions and learn how a slinky is used to heat things up.

title: HVAC-B Limit Switches
description: A limit switch is a safety device that will break the circuit between two specific terminals when a certain temperature is reached. This particular limit switch is adjustable and has a bi-metallic sensor that will open and closed based on the temperature setting. Watch this CTE video and learn the inner components of the limit switch and gain a better understanding of their operation.

title: HVAC-B Hot Surface Igniter
description: A hot surface igniter, also known as a glow plug, is a device used in a gas heat operation. Depending on the type of unit you are using, they can be run on different voltages. These devices have a very simple operation. You simply run the correct voltage through in order to heat it up. Watch this CTE video with Robert Currie and learn how this device is used to ignite a heating system.

title: HVAC-B Wet Switches
description: While not always a component of an air conditioning system, a wet switch is something used often in warm humid climates. In this climate drains and water leaks can pose a serious problem for home owners. A wet switch simply sits on the floor below the unit and senses moisture. It is wired into the system in order to shut down the condensing unit in the event of a water leak. This device is a simple way to prevent catastrophic water damage to a home.

title: HVAC-B Heat Strips
description: A heat strip is an electric resistance heater that is used in many applications of air handlers or heat pumps. Just like a space heater, the basic operation of this device is to push electrical current through coils which in turn begin to heat up. In this CTE video on heat strips you'll learn the major components, how they operate and the many different specifications they can run under.

title: HVAC-B Thermostatic Expansion Valves
description: Also known as a TXV, the Thermostatic Expansion Valve. This valve is located inside of the evaporator coil on an air handler or even just a standard coil. What the Thermostatic Expansion Valve does is measure the flow of refrigerant through the evaporator coil to ensure the proper amount. Watch this CTE video on Thermostatic Expansion Valve with Robert Currie from Innovative Air Solutions and learn the components that make up this device, it's purpose and how it functions.

title: HVAC-B Dampers
description: A damper is something that has a depressing, subduing, or inhibiting effect. In other words, a device that holds something back. A damper in an HVAC system has a specific purpose, especially in a zone system. A zone system is one where you can have multiple thermostats in one system that is able to control the air flow in one area or the other. They way a damper fits into to this is by cutting into a duct and inserting it in order to control the air flow. In this video Robert is discussing an opposed blade damper as a high end device to control air flow in zone system.

title: HVAC-B Damper Motors
description: In a previous CTE video we discussed the use of an opposed blade damper in a zone system. These dampers must be controlled by a motor. Can you guess what this motor is called. That's right, a damper motor. There may be many choices in which damper motors to choose but in this CTE video you'll learn how important it is for you to have the correct one.
